stem: Priya deposits Rs 8,000 in a savings scheme that pays simple interest at 9% per annum. What is the total interest she earns after 3 years?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Using T = 4 instead of 3 gives 8000 * 9 * 4 / 100 = 2880, misreading the number of years.
Dividing P*R = 720 by 3 rather than multiplying, i.e. computing 8000 * 9 / 100 * (10/3) ~ 2400; the wrong formula path gives 8000 * 10 * 3 / 100 = 2400 (using 10% instead of 9%).
Computing interest for only 1 year: 8000 * 9 * 1 / 100 = 720, dropping the 3-year period.

explanation_sections.punchline: SI accumulates linearly: every year adds the same fixed amount P*R/100.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: SI = P*R*T/100. Map givens: P = 8000, R = 9% p.a., T = 3 years. Substitute directly. No period conversion needed because rate and time are both annual.
explanation_sections.lesson: In SI the total interest is directly proportional to time; doubling T doubles SI.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 s. Eliminate option 4 (only 1 year of interest) and option 2 (4 years) by inspection; choose between 1 and 3 by checking 9% not 10%.
